body: `should_rotate()` subtracts `now` (timezone-aware UTC) from `created` parsed via `datetime.fromisoformat(created_at)`. If `created_at` ever lacks a timezone offset (naive datetime from an older secret payload or manual edits), this will raise `TypeError` and break the rotation cron. Consider normalizing naive `created` values (e.g., assume UTC) or validating `created_at` to fail with a clearer error.

author: Copilot
body: Initialization writes the new key to Secrets Manager before attempting the NOC upload. If the upload fails, the handler raises and leaves a non-empty active secret, so later deploy/cron runs will treat the environment as initialized and won’t retry uploading that same key (only a forced rotation that generates a different key). This can strand an environment where filers encrypt for a key Portal never published. Consider persisting an explicit “noc_uploaded” flag and retrying uploads when false, or adding an idempotent re-upload path that doesn’t generate a new key.

author: nick-falco
body: Won't fix - encryption is mandatory. `AWSCloudCredentials.__init__` is lazy (just stores the ARN; STS isn't called until the first `get_auth_headers()`), so an empty ARN doesn't break import or Lambda cold-start. The failure only surfaces when `encrypt_for_filer()` actually tries to fetch a key, which is the correct behavior- feature stacks shouldn't silently skip encryption. Adding a disable path creates dead code we'd have to remove later.

author: nick-falco
body: Good fix. The key rotation Lambda runs on a daily cron. A single transient NOC failure shouldn't leave an environment in a permanently broken state that requires manual intervention. With this fix, the next cron run self-heals.

author: Copilot
body: `_unwrap_b64_transport()` base64-decodes any base64-looking body. After `sqs_lambda_handler`’s SNS binary unwrapping, the normal NBN payload is already a zstd+base64 *string*; decoding it again will produce zstd bytes, which then get passed into `try_decrypt()` and can break the unencrypted path (UnicodeDecodeError) and/or decompression. Update the unwrap logic to only return decoded `bytes` when the decoded blob is actually a binary PGP message (e.g., `is_pgp_message(raw_bytes)`), otherwise return the original string (or decoded UTF-8 string) to avoid double-decoding the already-base64 payload.

author: Copilot
body: `try_decrypt()` currently does `raw.decode('utf-8')` for non-PGP `bytes`. If a non-encrypted payload ever arrives as non-UTF8 bytes (e.g., decoded compressed bytes), this will raise `UnicodeDecodeError` and fail the whole message. Consider catching `UnicodeDecodeError` here and either (a) returning a base64-encoded string, or (b) raising a `DecryptionError` with a clear message indicating the payload is non-text and not PGP, so failures are actionable.

author: nick-falco
body: The concern's premise that `event.body` is already the unwrapped zstd+base64 string is incorrect. `sqs_lambda_handler`doesn't touch NBN's base64 layer.

author: nick-falco
body: Dismissing. The `raw.decode("utf-8")` UnicodeDecodeError would only fire for corrupt or completely unexpected data. It is not a real-world code path.

These roles also appear as CloudFormation outputs in the NOC building-blocks stacks (`NocKeyServiceROAccessRoleARN` and `NocKeyServiceAllAccessRoleARN`).  The roles trust principals matching `arn:aws:iam::<portal-account>:role/portal-eventhub-{env}*-key-rotation-role`. 

For now I propose leaving this as is and potentially creating a follow up story to change this to use the building blocks env vars at a future date. Right now this matches how we do this other places.

author: Copilot
body: In the inline-payload path, `body = _unwrap_b64_transport(event.body)` can yield `bytes` for valid (but non-UTF8) decoded data; passing that into `try_decrypt()` will raise on the non-PGP path (`raw.decode('utf-8')`). After tightening `_unwrap_b64_transport` to only decode when the decoded data is PGP, `body` should remain a `str` for the normal zstd+base64 payload so `_decode_body()` can successfully decompress it.

author: nick-falco
body: If somehow non-UTF-8 non-PGP bytes arrived, the `.decode("utf-8")` would raise - but that's correct behavior (fail loudly on corrupted/unexpected data rather than silently passing garbage through).

body: The doc says outbound appliance public keys are cached "in-memory with a 5-minute TTL". In the implementation, OutboundEncryptionService uses TenantCacheService (Redis) when provided (and only falls back to an in-process dict when no cache service is supplied). Please update this section to reflect Redis-backed tenant-scoped caching (and mention the in-memory fallback only for non-runtime/test usage).
